english.title: Channel tunnel - damage goods
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and intentionally damaged goods, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS..), on a Channel Tunnel train, namely **(..SPECIFY TRAIN..), so as to

(A)_[endanger]_
(B)_[be likely to endanger]_

(C)_[the safe operation of the train]_
(D)_[the safety of the tunnel system]_
english.legislation: Contrary to article 6(1)(b) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
unlawfully intentionally damaged goods on a channel tunnel train
endanger the safe operation of the train
likely to endanger the safe operation of the train
endanger the safety of the tunnel system
likely to endanger the safety of the tunnel system

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required, see article 9(1) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994.
(ii) See also offence wordings H1106, H1371 and H1372.
(iii) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.penalty:
Life imprisonment.
